info.title: dr-strange JSON-RPC
info.description:
The wire protocol served by `drsg serve` (arch/08). Every method maps 1:1 to the core API. This document is the source of truth for the language SDKs and doubles as the RPC reference; the server returns it verbatim from `rpc.discover`.

Auth: the whole surface is authenticated. Send the shared token as `Authorization: Bearer <DRSG_TOKEN>` over HTTP (or `?token=` on the WebSocket). With no token configured on the server, only the same-origin browser UI may call it. An unauthenticated call fails with error code -32001.

Each method carries an `x-access` tag (read | write | admin): the tier a scoped key would need. Under the single shared token all three tiers require the same token.

A write may fail with -32002 when it waited out `[server] write_timeout_secs` for the single writer slot, which one long import or digest can hold. It is the one error worth retrying unchanged: nothing was attempted and the request was not wrong.

x-error-codes.-32000: application error (bad plane, dangling edge endpoint, conflict, …)
x-error-codes.-32002: write timed out waiting for the writer slot (retryable)

x-websocket.description: The `/ws` endpoint answers these request/response methods AND a change-feed subscription (ROADMAP §5). Send `plane.watch` to start receiving `plane.change` notifications for a plane; `plane.unwatch` to stop. Best-effort: a subscriber that falls too far behind drops events. These are WebSocket-only (not in the HTTP dispatch table).

params.label: string (optional) — only node changes carrying this label; edges pass only when omitted

params.changes: [{ kind: node|edge, op: created|updated|deleted, id, labels?, record? }] — record is the sanitized node/edge (no embeddings, no _-prefixed props); a delete carries id only

methods.name: rpc.discover
methods.summary: This OpenRPC service description.

methods.name: db.stats
methods.summary: Plane/node/edge counts plus the on-disk file size when persistent.

methods.name: db.catalog
methods.summary: The soft-schema catalog rolled up across every plane.

methods.name: plugin.list
methods.summary: Installed preprocessor plugins — the same records `drsg plugin list --json` prints, so an agent reads one shape from either surface (ROADMAP §11).

methods.name: plugin.catalog
methods.summary: The official plugin catalog this build pins: release-tagged URLs and their artifact SHA-256 hashes. A constant of the binary, not a network lookup — join against plugin.list to tag entries installed/upgradable/absent.

claims.description: Claimed extensions as display text, e.g. ".ts .tsx"

url.description: Release-tagged download URL; the artifact at it never changes

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the artifact at url

methods.name: plugin.install
methods.summary: Download, validate, hash-pin and store a plugin from an http(s) URL. Write-gated; the URL passes the same resolved-address network policy as every other fetch. Server-local paths are deliberately not accepted over RPC.

methods.name: plugin.remove
methods.summary: Uninstall a plugin by name. Write-gated.

methods.name: plane.list
methods.summary: Every plane with its id, name, counts, and own properties.

methods.name: plane.vectorize
methods.summary: Embed every node in a plane (incremental by meaning — unchanged texts are skipped) and ensure a vector index on `embedding` per label. Same engine as `drsg vectorize`; the provider key comes from the server's environment.

schema.description: Provider preset or base URL (default openai)

methods.name: plane.catalog
methods.summary: One plane's soft schema (labels, property descriptions, edge types, counts).

methods.name: node.get
methods.summary: One node by id or external key; null if absent.

schema.description: Omit vector-valued properties (replaced by a `$vector(N dims, omitted)` marker) — the agent shape. Default false: existing callers see the full records.

methods.name: plane.neighbors
methods.summary: 1-hop expansion as {node, edge} id pairs.

params.name: as_of
params.description: Time-travel: pin the read to this past commit sequence (native backend only).

params.name: as_of_ms
params.description: Time-travel: pin the read to the latest commit at or before this unix-epoch millisecond (native backend only).

methods.name: plane.history
methods.summary: Time-travel window: oldest and latest commit sequences a read can be pinned to (native backend only).

methods.name: plane.search
methods.summary: Vector top-k over a property; returns scored node records.

methods.name: plane.query
methods.summary: Run a serialized logical plan verbatim; returns scored rows.

params.name: as_of
params.description: Time-travel: run the plan against this past commit sequence (native backend only).

params.name: as_of_ms
params.description: Time-travel: run the plan against the latest commit at or before this unix-epoch millisecond (native backend only).

methods.name: plane.cypher
methods.summary: Run a statement in the query language (openCypher subset). A read returns {nodes, edges, count}; a write (CREATE/MERGE/SET/REMOVE/DELETE) returns {write: true, ...change-counts}. Write-gated.

schema.description: Embedding provider for a text SEARCH ... NEAR "..." (default openai); key from the server env.
Values for $name placeholders in the query (no string interpolation).
Omit vector-valued properties (replaced by a `$vector(N dims, omitted)` marker) — the agent shape. Default false: existing callers see the full records.
Read: {nodes, edges, count}. Write: {write, nodes_created, edges_created, props_set, labels_set, nodes_deleted, edges_deleted}.

methods.name: plane.find
methods.summary: Text (or semantic) search over the plane's nodes and edges.

params.name: as_of
params.description: Time-travel: search this past commit sequence (native backend only). Semantic search brute-forces the snapshot, since the vector index reflects only the latest commit.

params.name: as_of_ms
params.description: Time-travel: search the latest commit at or before this unix-epoch millisecond (native backend only).

methods.name: plane.algo
methods.summary: Run a graph algorithm (pagerank | components | shortest_path | louvain) over the plane or one label subset, read-only over a single snapshot.

schema.description: pagerank/louvain/components: {algo, results, count}. shortest_path: {algo, found, path:{nodes, edges, cost}|null}.

methods.name: plane.hybrid
methods.summary: Hybrid retrieval: fuse vector similarity, BM25 keyword, and graph-proximity channels into one ranking. Enable a channel by naming its property (vector_prop/keyword_prop) or setting graph_hops; the vector channel embeds q server-side.

methods.name: plane.ask
methods.summary: Natural-language query: an LLM turns the question into a read-only LogicalPlan, runs it (unless dry_run), and returns the generated plan plus result node records. With embed_provider, the model can call find_edge/find_entity embedding tools to ground the plan. Keys from the server env.

schema.description: {plans:[plan…], ran, attempts, results:[node…], edges:[edge…], count} — the generated plan(s) and their unioned matched subgraph (nodes + connecting edges).

methods.name: plane.indexes
methods.summary: The search indexes declared on a plane (vector + keyword), so a client can offer only the channels that actually exist.

methods.name: index.ensure
methods.summary: Declare (and build) a search index on (label, property): a keyword (BM25) or vector (embedding) index. Idempotent.

methods.name: graph.seed
methods.summary: An initial canvas of nodes plus induced edges. `order` seeds the highest-ranked nodes rather than the first the scan reaches — a legible skeleton instead of an arbitrary sample — and returns the scores alongside, so a caller can size or weight by importance without a second call.

params.name: order
params.summary: `degree` or `pagerank` seed the plane's important nodes instead of the first ones the scan reaches, and return their scores. Prefer `degree` for a skeleton: PageRank pools rank in sinks, so a hub can rank below its own neighbours.

params.name: as_of
params.description: Time-travel: seed from this past commit sequence (native backend only).

params.name: as_of_ms
params.description: Time-travel: seed from the latest commit at or before this unix-epoch millisecond (native backend only).

methods.name: graph.expand
methods.summary: Hub-safe 1-hop neighbourhood around a node: neighbour + connecting-edge records.

params.name: as_of
params.description: Time-travel: expand within this past commit sequence (native backend only).

params.name: as_of_ms
params.description: Time-travel: expand within the latest commit at or before this unix-epoch millisecond (native backend only).

methods.name: digest.run
methods.summary: Extract a node/edge proposal from text via the LLM (dry-run; spends provider credits). `mode` sets how much clean-up follows the extraction: `coarse` reconciles the label and edge-type vocabularies, `fine` (the default) also merges entities that name the same thing, `super` also re-reads every entity against all the passages mentioning it — most accurate, and ~15x the input token usage.

params.name: mode
params.summary: How thoroughly to clean up the extraction, trading cost for precision. `coarse` reconciles the label and edge-type vocabularies, which chunks read independently never converge on. `fine` (the default) also merges entities that name the same thing and checks every key against the graph exactly, so a re-digest links rather than duplicating. `super` also re-reads every entity against all the passages mentioning it, repairing properties that one-round extraction fixed from whichever chunk mentioned it first — the most accurate, and by far the most expensive (~15x input token usage), since every eligible entity carries its passages into a call of its own.

methods.name: digest.write
methods.summary: Write a previously-computed proposal into the plane via the bulk path (no LLM call).

methods.name: node.create
methods.summary: Add a node with an optional stable external key and labels.

methods.name: node.update
methods.summary: Patch a node: `set`/`unset` its properties, and `labels` (when present) replaces its label set.

methods.name: node.delete
methods.summary: Delete a node and cascade to its incident edges.

methods.name: edge.create
methods.summary: Add a directed edge between two existing nodes (each named by id or key).

methods.name: edge.update
methods.summary: Patch an edge: `set`/`unset` its properties, and `type` (when present) changes its type.

methods.name: edge.delete
methods.summary: Delete one edge.

methods.name: plane.create
methods.summary: Make a new, empty plane.

methods.name: plane.rename
methods.summary: Rename an existing plane.

methods.name: plane.set_props
methods.summary: Replace a plane's own property map.

methods.name: plane.delete
methods.summary: Drop a plane and everything on it (the startup plane cannot be dropped).

Properties.description: Property map in the core JSON dialect: scalars map directly; {"$vector":[…]} is an embedding; {"$desc":…,"$value":…} is a described value.

NodeRef.description: A node reference: a numeric id or an external key.

match.description: Present on plane.find hits: which field matched.

labels.description: Distinct node labels across all planes.

edge_types.description: Distinct edge types across all planes.

commit_seq.description: The current commit sequence (total committed writes).
